decisions.statement: A fixture holds what a test is set up with rather than what a test proves.
The scaffolding one module's tests alone need sits beside that module instead.
A test or another fixture is what reaches a fixture.
A fixture's own test proves the fixture rather than the system.
A fixture holds no fixtures of its own.
A fixture nothing but fixtures' own tests reach is unused code.
A fixture has the page that fixture needs rather than restating its values.
A fixture invents a page only where no page represents what the test needs.
A page a fixture invents has a slug no page in the tree has.
A fixture stating the values of a page it does not import has nothing keeping the two alike.
A fixture sits in a world the system could have built.
Nothing says a fixture has fallen behind the system that fixture feeds.
A system reading the pages' declarations refuses a world declaring no property unique.

definition: the world more than one module's tests are set up with

directives.name: Carry The Real Page
directives.act: Import the page a fixture needs into the fixture tree rather than restating its values.
directives.warrant: A restated page falls behind what the pages declare, and every test keeps passing while it does.
aids: A page is a module, so a fixture can import it.
Invent a page only where none represents what the test needs.
A fixture missing what the code derives from answers empty rather than wrong.
